This item attaches stability predicates to two explicitly stated model
classes. **(a) Framework force models:** an autonomous model of
[[def-cm16-flow-equilibria-and-invariant-sets]] clauses (i)-(ii), with open
state domain $S_0\subseteq\mathbb R^{6N}$, associated field
$G:S_0\to\mathbb R^{6N}$ and its maximal-solution local flow
$\Phi:\Omega\to S_0$ ([[def-cm-local-flow-of-an-autonomous-system]]).
**(b) Mechanical chart models:** the data $(\Omega,M,U)$ of
[[def-cm-mechanical-vector-field-and-energy-in-a-chart]], where
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is open, $M$ is a $C^2$ positive-definite
matrix field, and $U$ is $C^2$; here the state domain is
$S_0:=\Omega\times\mathbb R^n$, the state dimension is $m:=2n$, and the
associated mechanical field is $G:S_0\to\mathbb R^m$. It is $C^1$, hence
continuous and locally Lipschitz, and has the local flow and maximal solutions
of [[def-cm-local-flow-of-an-autonomous-system]]. For class (a) only the
standing continuous, state-locally-Lipschitz regularity is required for
clauses (i)-(ii); clauses (iii)-(iv) add $C^1$ regularity explicitly. In each
application the predicates concern the declared model objects and quantify
over its maximal solutions; the two model classes are not being identified.

**Numerical state metric.** All norms and balls below apply to dimensionless
numerical coordinates. For class (a) these are the SI numerical coordinates
of [[def-cm16-flow-equilibria-and-invariant-sets]] clause (iv). For class (b),
fix a positive duration reference $t_{\rm ref}$ and a positive reference
quantity $a_j$ of the dimension of each configuration coordinate, and read
$q_j=Q_j/a_j$, $v_j=V_j/(a_j/t_{\rm ref})$ and $t=t_{\rm phys}/t_{\rm ref}$;
thus $q'=v$. The given mathematical chart data $M,U,G$ are the numerical
data in this chart. For either class the distance is
$d(z,z')=\bigl(\sum_j(q_j-q_j')^2+\sum_j(v_j-v_j')^2\bigr)^{1/2}$,
with $q=x$ in class (a). The same convention applies to tangent vectors
and to clause (v)'s numerical map charts. Different positive reference
scales give equivalent norms: their ratios are bounded above and below by
the largest and smallest diagonal scale ratios. Hence they preserve the
stability, convergence and boundedness predicates, while quantitative
radii and bounds can change.

**(ii) Orbital stability of an invariant set.** Let $S\subseteq S_0$ be a
nonempty compact set invariant under the selected model's local flow $\Phi$;
that is, $(t,z)\in\Omega$ for every $z\in S$ and $t\in\mathbb R$, and
$\Phi_t(S)=S$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. For the framework force-model
class this is clause (iv) of
[[def-cm16-flow-equilibria-and-invariant-sets]]. The Euclidean orbital
distance is $d(z,S):=\inf_{s\in S}\lVert z-s\rVert_2$. Then $S$ is
**orbitally stable** when for every open set
$U\supseteq S$ there is an open set $V$ with $S\subseteq V\subseteq U$ such
that every maximal solution $z$ with $z(0)\in V$ is defined for all $t\ge0$
and satisfies $z(t)\in U$ for all $t\ge0$. Orbital stability is a statement
about the set, not about one motion, and it does not assert attraction.

**(vi) Distinctions.** (a) The predicates in clauses (i)-(v) have different
definitions and are not interchangeable. In particular, Lyapunov stability
does not by definition include attraction, and orbital stability is a
property of a set rather than of one of its points. Hyperbolicity alone does
not imply linear instability: if all eigenvalues of $DG(z_*)$ have negative
real part, the stable estimate of
[[thm-cm-exponential-dichotomy-for-a-hyperbolic-endomorphism]] makes every
solution of the variational equation decay and hence remain bounded. If a
hyperbolic equilibrium has an eigenvalue with positive real part, the same
dichotomy supplies an unbounded forward solution and the equilibrium is
linearly unstable. (b) At
an equilibrium the spectrum of $DG(z_*)$ is invariant under a $C^2$ chart
transition, by the similarity formula in
[[def-cm16-flow-equilibria-and-invariant-sets]] clause (vi)(b); norms and
finite-time growth bounds can depend on the chart. (c) For the
mechanical chart data $(M,U)$ of
[[def-cm-mechanical-vector-field-and-energy-in-a-chart]], at a mechanical
equilibrium $(q_0,0)$ the derivative of the field is
$DG(q_0,0)(\delta q,\delta v)=(\delta v,-M(q_0)^{-1}D^2U(q_0)\delta q)$; the
stability consequences of that computation are proved later on the page.

**(i) The stroboscopic map.** Let a $P$-periodic stability model be fixed
($P>0$; [[def-cm16-flow-equilibria-and-invariant-sets]] clause (i)). Its
restriction domain $D\subseteq\mathbb R\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ is
invariant under time shifts by $P$. Define its time-zero state slice
$$S_P:=\{z_0\in Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}:(0,z_0)\in D\};$$
periodicity gives the same admissible slice at every integer multiple of $P$.
For $z_0\in S_P$, let $z_D(\cdot;z_0):I^D_{z_0}\to
Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ be the unique $D$-maximal state curve through $z_0$ at
time $0$, with interval $I^D_{z_0}$ as in
[[def-cm16-flow-equilibria-and-invariant-sets]] clause (i). The
**stroboscopic map at period $P$** is the partial map
$$\Psi:\Sigma\longrightarrow S_P,\qquad \Sigma:=\{z_0\in S_P:[0,P]\subseteq I^D_{z_0}\},\qquad \Psi(z_0):=z_D(P;z_0),$$
with domain $\Sigma$ the states whose $D$-maximal motion remains in the
declared restriction domain throughout $[0,P]$. Its endpoint belongs to
$S_P$ because the restriction domain is preserved by the shift from $P$ to
$0$. Its **iterates** are defined
recursively by $\Psi^1:=\Psi$ and, where
$\Psi^n(z_0)\in\Sigma$, $\Psi^{n+1}(z_0):=\Psi(\Psi^n(z_0))$; the domain of
$\Psi^n$ is therefore the set of states whose $D$-maximal motion remains in
$D$ over $[0,nP]$, and it may be strictly smaller than $\Sigma$. This domain
identity follows by induction from the $P$-periodicity of the field, shift
invariance of $D$ and uniqueness of the $D$-maximal solution. A state
$z_*\in\Sigma$ with $\Psi(z_*)=z_*$ is a **fixed point** of $\Psi$. It is a
**$P$-periodic state** in the full-time sense: the motion through $z_*$ extends
to a motion on $\mathbb R$ satisfying $z(t+P)=z(t)$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$.
Indeed, write the state curve on $[0,P]$ as $z_*(t)$; for $k\in\mathbb Z$ and
$s\in[0,P]$ set $\widetilde z(kP+s):=z_*(s)$. The endpoint states agree
because $z_*(P)=z_*(0)$, and the vector field agrees at the seams by its
$P$-periodicity. The restriction domain is preserved by those time shifts, so
the translated segments solve the same equation; uniqueness glues them to a
global motion. No completeness of $\Psi$ is asserted: $\Sigma$ need not be all
of $S_P$, and iterates can leave the domain.

**(ii) Autonomous special case.** If the model is autonomous, then its
stroboscopic map at any period $P>0$ is the time-$P$ map $\Phi_P$ of its local
flow restricted to $\Omega_P=\{z\in S_0:(P,z)\in\Omega\}$
([[def-cm16-flow-equilibria-and-invariant-sets]] clause (ii)); this is the
reading used for the isotropic-oscillator check on the page.
